To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Hypercube networks with a large number of faulty (nonfunctional) nodes are locally subcube connected with high probability; and (2) Locally subcube-connected hypercubes are efficiently and effectively routable with local-information-based routing algorithms.
(1) hypercube networks with up to 37 percent faulty nodes remain connected with high probability and (2) routing on such connected networks can be done in linear time.
hypercube networks are highly robust against node failures and that routing algorithms on such networks are efficient and distributed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a very large class of hypercube networks that may contain a very large number (as high as 37.5% of the total number) of faulty nodes.

the design of a fault-tolerant network architecture that is highly scalable and efficient in terms of the number of faulty nodes it can tolerate and the time and length of the routing paths it can construct.
a class of hypercube networks with very large number of failures, which are not only locally subcube-connected but also have a distributed and local-information based routing capability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hypercube network is a very reliable network architecture.
the local subcube-connected hypercubes are a very robust and reliable interconnection structure for massively parallel computers.

, for any given hypercube network that contains a very large number (up to 37. 5 percent) of faulty nodes, if the remaining nonfaulty subnetwork is locally subcube-connected then the network remains connected, and our routing algorithm can find a routing path between any two nonfaulty nodes of length bounded by 4 times their Hamming distance, and the algorithm runs in linear time and is distributed and local information based.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for hypercube networks with up to 37, 5 percent faulty nodes and a large number of nodes, a simple and natural condition can be identified under which the network still remains connected, and routing algorithms can be developed to find routing paths in a distributed and localized manner.
, for a very large number, up to 37 percent, of node failures, a locally subcube-connectivity condition can be maintained in a distributed and localized manner.

, for hypercube networks with up to 37 percent faulty nodes, the local subcubec-connectivity condition is satisfied with a very high probabability and our routing algorithms can find routing paths of nearly minimal length in linear time, which are optimal in both time complexity and path length.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a hypercube network that is locally subcube-connected, it can still be connected even when a large number of nodes fail.
hypercube networks are very robust against node failures and that the robustness can be maintained in a distributed and localized way.
, under the local subcube-connected condition, hypercube networks with up to 37 percent faulty nodes can still remain connected, which is much higher than the previously known upper bound.
